title: The Night Shift
logline: On steep, misted hill roads, an ambulance crew races between a district hospital and villages that are sometimes twenty minutes away and sometimes two hours, and every call is a small argument with time.
human_question: How much difference can skill and speed make against how fragile a life actually is?

premise.story: One long overnight shift with a rural ambulance crew, following whatever calls actually come in.
premise.place: A hill-district ambulance service covering winding roads between a base hospital and outlying villages.
premise.experience: Headlights on wet mountain roads, the particular tension of a call coming in, first aid given at the roadside or in a home, and the crew's own account, between calls, of what the job has taught them.

concept_links.why: The source names carelessness, unsuitable conditions and untreated illness among the ordinary causes of an early death, and says a death that seemed to be coming could sometimes still be averted by skilled help [C060-P:L62-L66; C060-M:L29-L33]. A crew's working night is exactly where that skill and that fragility meet.

what_camera_could_observe: The drive on narrow hill roads
First aid given at a scene
The crew's own reflections at shift's end
what_must_be_real: The crew's real working shift. Patients in crisis are protected; no identifiable patient is shown without explicit consent, and no death is filmed.

possible_arc.opening: The crew starting a shift, checking equipment.
possible_arc.turn: A call that tests everything they have.
possible_arc.ending_open: Dawn and the end of shift, whatever the night actually brought.

requirements: A rural or hill-district ambulance service willing to permit filming under strict patient-privacy conditions
A crew willing to be followed for at least one full shift

suggestions.name: The Badulla or Nuwara Eliya district hill roads
suggestions.why: Winding hill roads and dispersed villages of the kind this story needs; no specific service identified.
suggestions.verify: No ambulance service or crew confirmed; health authority permission would be required.

risks: Patient privacy and dignity in emergencies
Accident and injury risk to the crew while filming
drop_if: No ambulance service grants filming access under safe privacy conditions
A shift produces nothing filmable without compromising patient care

connections.note: Both follow someone called to where death may be near, one racing to prevent it, one accompanying it when it cannot be prevented.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
